entries.title: Background
entries.content: Following the Appellate Division's 4 July 2024 ruling upholding the High Court's order, protests intensified. From July 7 to 10, 2024, students carried out the “Bangla Blockade”: thousands boycotted classes and blocked major highways, railways, and intersections across the country, including Shahbagh in Dhaka, causing severe disruption to traffic for several days running. On 10 July 2024, the Supreme Court temporarily suspended the quota ruling for one month following legal petitions — a partial concession. On the same day, the Rapid Action Battalion, a paramilitary force previously accused of serious human rights violations, was deployed alongside police to help contain the protests. The state was offering a concession and hardening its response at the same time.

entries.title: What Followed
entries.content: On 11 July 2024, police announced they would act against road blockades, arguing the suspension removed justification to continue. Tens of thousands of protesters defied this and kept blocking roads. The standoff between the partial concession and the continuing blockade set the stage for the next phase of the movement, a period covered in later chapters.
